---
title: "Pipeline reference"
description: "The keys in an .airway.yml file, the supported source kinds, and how credentials resolve"
---

An Airway pipeline is a `.airway.yml` file. Unknown top-level keys are a
parse error rather than being silently ignored, so a typo surfaces as soon as
the file is compiled.

## Keys

| Key | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | | The pipeline's name, which must be non-empty |
| `source` | yes | | `{ kind, config }`, where `kind` picks the connector and `config` holds its settings |
| `destination` | yes | | `{ database, dataset_name }`, naming a database from `config.yml` and the dataset (schema) to load into |
| `description` | no | | Free text |
| `resources` | no | all | A subset of the source's resources to load |
| `concurrency` | no | `1` | How many resources extract in parallel, up to `16` |
| `allow_concurrent_runs` | no | `false` | Lifts the one-run-at-a-time guard; set it only on a pipeline with no cursor and no replacing tables |
| `streaming` | no | `true` | Streams rows to the destination, falling back to bulk loading automatically |

Note that omitting `concurrency` means one resource at a time rather than
unlimited parallelism, so a pipeline with many resources that leaves it unset
runs correctly but slowly.

## Source kinds

Oxygen supports the following `kind` values. The field is free text, so an
unsupported kind parses cleanly and fails only when the pipeline runs, with
an `unsupported source kind` error.

| Category | Kinds |
| --- | --- |
| Restaurant and commerce | `toast`, `ubereats`, `sp_api` |
| Accounting and ERP | `quickbooks`, `netsuite` |
| Databases | `sql_database`, `postgres_cdc`, `clickhouse` |
| Files and sheets | `http_file`, `filesystem`, `google_sheets` |
| Public and geographic data | `weather`, `besttime`, `overture`, `overpass` |
| Anything with an HTTP API | `rest_api` |

`rest_api` is the general-purpose connector: most vendor APIs without a
dedicated kind can be described directly as a `rest_api` config, so a
missing kind is rarely a blocker.

## Credentials

Credentials live in the workspace's secret manager and never in the YAML. A
config key ending in `_var` names a secret **key** rather than holding a
value, and Oxygen substitutes the secret's value at run time:

```yaml
source:
  kind: toast
  config:
    client_id_var: TOAST_CLIENT_ID
    client_secret_var: TOAST_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each kind manages its own set of `_var` keys, and those sets do not overlap,
so copy them from an example for the same kind rather than borrowing from
another. `rest_api` nests its credentials under `auth` instead:

```yaml
source:
  kind: rest_api
  config:
    auth:
      type: api_key_query
      key_var: CENSUS_API_KEY
      param: key
```

## Destinations

Pipelines load into a database declared in `config.yml`. In practice this is
almost always an [Airhouse](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airhouse)
database declared as `airhouse_managed`, which mints credentials at run time
so the pipeline never holds a warehouse password; Postgres destinations are
also supported.
